ownership_reason: Only the gold builds the root of the name together with its properties; hop 1 splits the name, hop 2 counts the parts and hops 3-4 pass them along, and each gets back one finished tree. No part string makes the gold produce a THIS root, and replacing the root of a finished tree takes a search for the root and a replaceChild, which is more than a one-line change. The convention is pinned outside the gold: Node.getQualifiedName returns "this" for a THIS root (the inverse of the facade) and NodeTest.testQualifiedName expects GETPROP(THIS, b) to read "this.b"; Node.isQualifiedName names this.a as a qualified name (case THIS; NodeTest.testIsQualifiedName) while Node.isUnscopedQualifiedName excludes this.a (NAME roots only); NodeUtil.getRootOfQualifiedName, beside the facade, requires the root to be a NAME or a THIS node. The parser never produces a NAME node named "this", so GETPROP(NAME this, prop) is not the node of the qualified name this.prop.
